chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hashim al-Kitab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, Abu al-Husayn al-Kufi, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Barmaki narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

When the Eye oppresses the Eye, the killing of the Eye is by the hand of the fourth of the Eyes. When that occurs, the one who deserts him incurs the curse of Allah, the Angels, and all people. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, what is the Eye and the Eyes? He said: As for the Eye, it is my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib. As for the Eyes, they are his enemies, the fourth of them is the one who kills him unjustly and aggressively.

key_terms.الْخَاذِلُ: The one who deserts/fails to support
key_terms.الْعَيْنُ: The Eyes (plural, referring to the enemies of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Eye' and who are the 'Eyes' in this hadith from Ma'ani al-Akhbar?
ai.summary: In this rare meaning (gharib al-hadith) from Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'the Eye' for Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and 'the Eyes' for his adversaries, identifying the fourth enemy as the one who kills him unjustly. While interpretations vary between Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn, the text emphasizes the spiritual consequence for the 'deserter' (al-khadhil), who incurs the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people, highlighting the centrality of Ali's martyrdom in Shia eschatology.
